statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r equals the number of unordered pairs {a,b} of distinct labels with 1 <= a < b <= n such that Path(a,b) contains exactly one prime label. Equivalently, r is the number of valid paths, where a valid path is an unordered pair of distinct nodes {a,b} whose unique connecting path has exactly one prime among its node labels; endpoints are included, and {a,b} and {b,a} are the same path counted once.
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 100000. edges is a slice of length n-1. For every i with 0 <= i < len(edges), edges[i] has length 2, and if edges[i][0] = u and edges[i][1] = v then 1 <= u <= n, 1 <= v <= n, and u != v. The undirected graph with vertex set {1,...,n} and an edge between u and v for each entry [u,v] or [v,u] in edges is connected and acyclic, so it is a tree with n-1 edges. A label x in {1,...,n} is prime iff x >= 2 and no integer d with 2 <= d < x divides x. For distinct a,b in {1,...,n}, Path(a,b) denotes the set of node labels on the unique simple path from a to b in this tree, including both endpoints.

statement: Fix a prime label p in {1,...,n}. Delete from the tree all nodes whose labels are prime, including p. This leaves a forest on the non-prime labels. Let C(p) be the set of connected components of this forest that contain at least one neighbor of p in the original tree. For a component C in C(p), let s(C) be the number of nodes in C. Then the number V(p) from the prime-decomposition specification is exactly sum over C in C(p) of s(C) plus sum over unordered pairs {C,D} of distinct components in C(p) of s(C)*s(D). Consequently, whenever the function returns a result r, r equals the sum of these quantities over all prime p in {1,...,n}.

statement: If count_paths(n, edges) returns r and count_paths(n, edges2) returns r2, then r = r2. In particular, permuting the entries of edges or swapping the two coordinates inside any entry does not change the result.

Let edges2 be another slice of length n-1 satisfying the same conditions, and assume that for every pair of labels u,v, [u,v] occurs as an entry of edges in either order if and only if it occurs as an entry of edges2 in either order. Thus edges and edges2 represent the same undirected tree.
